nodes.purpose: Turns analog input into a steering angle, the angle into a heading rate and a board lean, and filters the resulting velocity through a surface-relative deadzone

nodes.purpose: Assembles the maximum speed a rider may reach each update from board stats, catch-up, boost, slowdown and wings, then slews the value that is actually enforced

cards.name: Steering angle to heading rate
cards.summary: Stick input ramps a steering angle, and above a speed floor that angle becomes a heading rate that is limited to a small increment per update
cards.behavior: Each update the stick is scaled into a steering target measured in angle counts, with an extra twist when the stick is pinned sideways and also pushed downward. The gap between target and current steering angle is divided by eight, except inside a narrow band where it is nudged by one so the angle still settles. Once the speed magnitude passes a floor, half the steering angle is multiplied by the board handling byte and divided by a constant to give a turn rate; the magnitude of the sideways speed left after the deadzone, biased and shifted down by seven, is squared and multiplied by the board cornering byte and then divided by that turn rate, producing a curvature that is pushed away from zero when it comes out too small and finally turned into a heading increment limited to a fixed cap per update. Below the floor the heading follows the stick directly, which is what lets an almost stopped rider pivot on the spot.

cards.name: Board lean and roll
cards.summary: The steering angle drives a lateral model sway while the roll angle chases a value built from speed and turn direction
cards.behavior: A lean target is built from the sine and cosine of the steering angle scaled by a constant, mirrored when the rider is travelling backwards, then the gap between that target and the current lateral model offset is clamped and added to the transform so the board sways rather than snapping. The roll then chases a step derived from the speed magnitude: the speed is capped, negated when the rider is reversed, multiplied by the steering angle, divided by a fixed divisor and shifted down nine more bits. That step is clamped, reduced by the current roll, clamped again and accumulated, and when the result falls inside a small deadband the roll is zeroed and a neutral animation plays. Otherwise the absolute roll selects one of two mirrored lean animations played at half the roll magnitude, so the visible lean saturates long before the roll value does.

cards.name: Angle relaxation per update
cards.summary: Roll, pitch and steering angles wrap into the signed range and relax toward zero with a different cap on the ground than in the air
cards.behavior: The routine first folds each stored angle into the signed half-turn window and then subtracts a portion of the current value, capped so that no update moves more than the cap. On the ground the roll and steering angles share a large cap and the lateral model offset relaxes by up to a larger clamp; airborne the three angles relax by a much smaller cap and the offset by an intermediate clamp. Because the relaxation runs after gravity and before position integration, a rider who releases the stick drifts back into a straight line instead of stopping abruptly, and a rider in the air keeps only a slow residual spin.

cards.name: Surface-relative velocity deadzone
cards.summary: Speed is rotated into the surface frame, each local axis loses its deadzone or is zeroed, then the result is rotated back
cards.behavior: The velocity is transformed by a matrix pair built from the surface normal so that forward lies along the slope, and any downward component of the local velocity is dropped. A second matrix aligns the local frame with the rider heading, and after that each horizontal component either has its deadzone subtracted or, when it does not exceed the deadzone, is set to zero. The deadzones come from the caller: the driving, sliding and trick-slide passes pass a fixed forward and backward value plus the board-dependent lateral value from the stat table, while the bounce pass passes a much larger value on all three axes so a rider settles quickly after a fall. The local forward component is returned so the caller can compare it with speed thresholds, and the filtered velocity is rotated back into world space.

cards.name: Speed cap and catch-up
cards.summary: Base speed, catch-up, boost bonus, slowdown and wings pass through clamps and a smoothed slew before the cap is enforced on velocity
cards.behavior: The cap starts at the value derived from board and character stats, and a CPU rider has a per-difficulty penalty subtracted. A catch-up term starts at a per-finish-position table value minus the stored adjustment, and a large bonus is added when the rider leads the leader by a fixed amount of lap progress. The term is clamped in both directions with different limits and accumulates into a stored adjustment that is then added to the cap. Wings replace the board gravity with a small fixed value, a boost state adds a flat bonus that is roughly eight times larger for the rocket than for the fan, and the sum is capped absolutely and then reduced by a quarter for each active slowdown level. The cap that is actually enforced is a separate smoothed value that slews toward the target with a much larger rise cap than fall cap, except during a rocket impulse which snaps it straight to the target. A flag on the rider halves the cap before the boost bonus is added, so a rider carrying that flag gets the boost bonus on top of half their normal ceiling.

cards.name: Board stat to physics conversion
cards.summary: Six small stat bytes per board and character pair are shifted, scaled and biased into the six physics values the rider uses
cards.behavior: Every board and character pair carries six unsigned bytes. The max speed byte is multiplied by a large constant, divided by a hundred and biased to give the base cap in world units; the handling and cornering bytes become turn-rate values with fixed biases; the lateral deadzone byte is shifted, scaled and biased into the velocity deadzone; and the gravity and acceleration bytes are shifted by different amounts, scaled and biased into the per-update gravity and the launch acceleration. A boss racer replaces the lateral deadzone with one large fixed value. Because the three shifts differ, one point of stat weight counts for very different amounts in speed, gravity and acceleration.

cards.name: Trick charge and ramp launch
cards.summary: Holding the trick input charges a counter, and the release turns charge plus board acceleration into a launch along the board plane
cards.behavior: While the jump input is held the charge counter grows by a fixed step until it reaches a ceiling. Releasing the input sets the phase flag and, when the charge is above the ceiling, queues the trick type read from the stick. The launch phase then stores two magnitudes: a horizontal one built from the charge plus the board acceleration, and a vertical rise that is negated when the rider is facing backwards and doubled when the stick is pinned fully to one side. It rotates a shared launch vector through the rider orientation and tilt matrices and adds the result to velocity, with the already-applied gravity added back to the vertical component so the launch height does not depend on the order in which gravity and the launch ran. At this revision the two magnitudes and the launch vector are still single stand-alone words rather than the original tables, so the horizontal impulse magnitude is not fully recovered.

cards.name: Spin rotation sweep
cards.summary: A spin advances the trick rotation at a starting rate that decays past the half-turn mark and stops at one full turn
cards.behavior: Starting a spin trick resets both trick rotation axes and seeds a per-update rotation rate. Each update that rate is added to the spin axis, and once the rotation has passed the half-turn mark with no queued follow-up its magnitude is reduced by a fixed step, so the spin opens fast and eases into its end. The sweep stops at one full turn, where the rate is cleared and either the trick-rotation flag is dropped or the behavior continues straight into the queued trick. Flips reuse the same curve on the other rotation axis, so one rotation profile covers every trick in the chain, and the composed transform is rebuilt from both axes each update.

cards.name: Trick score award tiers
cards.summary: Landing converts the accumulated trick chain into race gold and picks a reward sound from fixed score thresholds
cards.behavior: On landing the accumulated trick chain is added to the rider race gold, and a score display is raised for human riders. A reward sound is then chosen by comparing the chain total against a ladder of fixed thresholds, so a single small trick and a long chain are audibly different, and in one of the alternate race types a separate points total is awarded as skill points through its own ladder. Each new trick in a chain adds a per-slot base value plus a per-slot bonus, a repeat of a trick already in the chain is worth less than a fresh one, and completing the whole set of eight pays a large lump sum. Both running totals saturate at a maximum instead of overflowing, and the mask is cleared so the next chain starts fresh.

cards.name: Knockback impulse and drag
cards.summary: A hit clamps the shove, lifts the rider at a fixed rise and bleeds the horizontal speed by a constant fraction
cards.behavior: A collision knockback stores an impact angle and a strength, and the strength is clamped at a ceiling before it is written into the knockback velocity. The airborne phase copies that velocity into the rider speed, rescales the horizontal part to the same ceiling, and sets a fixed upward rise so the rider always leaves the ground. Gravity then pulls the rise down while the horizontal speed is reduced by a fixed fraction of itself every update, which is a constant-fraction drag rather than a linear deceleration, so a fast shove fades quickly and a slow one lingers. The rider turns toward the track direction while airborne and drops into a bounce chain once the ground is reached, with a per-instance heat timer that the player can shorten by working the stick.

cards.name: Stun gravity and bounce settle
cards.summary: Being stunned uses its own gravity and a stronger drag, and the following bounce removes the last of the speed
cards.behavior: While stunned the rider falls under a stun gravity that is smaller than the board gravity, turns toward the track centre line by a clamped increment each update, and loses horizontal speed by a fixed fraction of itself. On landing a short counter holds the rider in a bounce phase with the same stun gravity and a coarse deadzone on all three velocity axes, so the rider settles instead of skating away. When the bounce animation finishes and the remaining horizontal speed is under a small threshold the rider resumes normal driving; otherwise the counter keeps the bounce going. The recovery also halves the smoothed speed cap once, which is why a stunned rider stays slow for a moment after standing up.

cards.name: Track wall push-out
cards.summary: Three sample points around the board are resolved against wall geometry, with a growing radius while the rider is stunned
cards.behavior: Three points in the rider frame, one at the centre and one on each side, are tested against the track wall geometry, and a hit returns a push offset that is applied to the rider position and to the remaining sample points so the following tests do not start inside the wall. The centre point is tested at a larger radius than the two side points, which treats the nose of the board as wider than its edges. While the rider carries the stunned flag the tested radius grows by a fixed count per update up to a limit, which lets a rider being knocked around slip through geometry instead of getting pinned, and the flag is cleared once the test has run. A hit is also reported back to the caller so the behavior can abandon the current phase, and the second failure code reports that a sample sits below the local track surface, which is also treated as a hit.

cards.name: Three-point terrain alignment
cards.summary: Three points dropped onto the track give two edge vectors, whose cross product becomes the surface normal behind pitch and roll
cards.behavior: The rider position is first raised to the track height under it, and the airborne flag is cleared when contact is found. Three sample points taken from a pattern chosen by the rider attack state are each dropped onto the track and lifted to the sampled height whenever they would otherwise sit below it, then reduced to two edge vectors and normalised to a fixed scale. Their cross product gives a surface normal, normalised to the same scale and rotated into the rider heading frame. Pitch and roll come from fixed-point arctangents of the normal components, masked into the signed angle window, and a rotation about the pitch is written straight into the orientation transform, so the board planes onto the slope instead of hovering at a fixed angle.

cards.name: Chase camera rig
cards.summary: A rest distance behind the rider, an eased aim height and a ground clearance keep the chase view stable through jumps and landings
cards.behavior: The rig starts behind the rider along a fixed offset rotated by the rider heading, with a rest distance, a closest distance, an aim height and a rig height. Each update it copies the rider vertical movement with a clamp and eases the distance and the aim height toward their rest values by dividing the difference by a fixed factor, so a jump or a landing is absorbed rather than followed rigidly. The horizontal distance is pushed out to the rig height, the full distance is clamped into a band between the rest distance and the rest distance plus a slack, and the look-at point is lifted along the camera up axis by the aim height scaled to the matrix unit. A terrain query under that look-at point lifts the whole rig when the track would otherwise cut through it, and a look-back input mirrors the view so the rider sees behind.

cards.name: Boost and shield durations
cards.summary: Each boost and shield arms a state and runs on a fixed update counter that a hit clears
cards.behavior: Item activation is gated on the rider having no boost in progress. The rocket boost sets a start state chosen by the rider facing and writes a countdown; the speed fan sets its own forward or reverse state with a countdown twice as long; wings use a separate active flag with an even longer countdown, and invincibility uses its own timer with a sound cue. The boost counters are cleared whenever a hit reaction begins, so a hit cancels a boost instead of leaving it running underneath the stun. The rocket start state advances to a sustain state once the impulse has been applied, which is how the short launch push and the longer sustained push share one counter.

cards.name: CPU look-ahead target
cards.summary: A CPU rider aims at a point found by walking sector links with lane offsets and a capped look-ahead distance
cards.behavior: The CPU first projects its own position onto the current sector centre line, then walks the sector links forward, choosing the left or right link when the stored path preference says so, until the waypoint ahead is further away than a fixed look-ahead limit. If a step overshoots, the offset is shortened to the limit, which keeps the aim point inside the visible track instead of jumping past a corner. Lane position on a sector comes from a lateral factor scaled by a fixed amount and from a lane width multiplier, and the blend between a sector start and end centre point uses a fixed number of interpolation steps. A separate random threshold out of 256 decides how often the CPU takes a shortcut branch, and the whole walk collapses to the lift entry point on the last sector of a lap.

cards.name: Course lift entry gate
cards.summary: The lift at the bottom of a lap accepts one rider inside an activation radius and hands out boarding order
cards.behavior: The gate accepts a rider only when its shared state is ready, the rider is not on the final lap, and the rider has reached the finish zone of the current lap. Ground distance to the course lift entry point is compared with an activation radius; inside that radius the gate moves to active, the rider receives the next boarding order and a shared order counter is decremented, so riders board in the order they arrive rather than all at once. A second proximity test with a smaller radius reports whether a rider is merely near the lift without touching the gate state, and the driving code consults it before handing a CPU rider over to the lift-approach phase.

cards.name: Snow spray billboard lifetime
cards.summary: A spray puff is a few billboards with a fixed frame count, a fixed alpha fade per update and a halved velocity
cards.behavior: A spray puff is scheduled as a task that draws the same billboard on several viewports. Its starting alpha is fixed, and every unpaused update advances the asset frame, subtracts a fixed amount from alpha and moves the billboard by a velocity the spawner halved, so the puff slows and fades as it drifts. The task terminates itself after a fixed number of updates instead of waiting on a condition. The two-sided spray used under a turning board starts at an alpha jittered inside a small random band, moves both billboards together and lives one update longer than the single puff, which keeps paired puffs from looking perfectly synchronised.
